seasonal year is not a leap year, adjust the date to February 28th.

logic.

Description
In fixed-position extract files, space padding is applied based on byte length rather than character
count.
When the data contains multilingual characters (for example, Chinese), this results in fields not 
occupying the expected number of character positions.
As a result, although the extract completes successfully, the output file may appear visually 
misaligned when reviewed, leading to concerns about field positioning.
Steps To Recreate
1.Configure an extract batch using a fixed-position format (FIXD).
2.Populate one or more fields of table being queried with multilingual (Unicode) characters.
3.Run the extract to generate the output file.
4.Review the generated file in a text editor.
Output:
The column containing multilingual characters ends before its expected position.

Description
Starting with 25.10, stricter validation was introduced for file names and extensions uploaded 
through the system (including batch driven uploads and attachments).
As part of this enhancement, the framework validates file extensions against a managed content 
allowlist (F1-FileExtensionAllowList).
After upgrading to 25.10, customers reported that certain file extensions that were previously 
accepted are now rejected during batch processing.
This fix is to introduce support for implementations to add to the system's allowlist for file 
extensions.
Steps To Recreate
1. Upload a file attachment from the "Add Attachment" page.
2. Ensure the extension being used is not present in managed content F1-FileExtensionAllowList.
3. Observe that the upload process rejects the file due to extension validation failure.

Reported Issue
Description
After upgrading CC&B from 2.7 to 25.4, billing behavior changed for Customer Class Bill Eligibility 
algorithms. In 2.7, these eligibility algorithms executed only once per account during billing, and if 
any eligibility algorithm encountered an error and created a To Do, the bill segment creation was 
rolled back, and eligibility processing stopped.
In the current version, the same eligibility algorithms are executed multiple times for the same 
account - typically once per billable Service Agreement (SA) within the account - because the 
billing process loops through SAs and repeatedly calls the billing routine that evaluates eligibility. 
Additionally, error handling differs when an eligibility algorithm creates a To Do, billing is not 
rolled back and subsequent eligibility algorithms continue to run, allowing billing to proceed.

Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing Bug 39011549 Product Fix Design
Batch Logs indicate that the Customer Class – Bill Eligibility algorithm was executed 3 times once 
for each SA.
Expected Result: The Bill Eligibility algorithms must be executed only once for the account 
irrespective of the number of service agreements it has. 
Actual Result: On the batch logs, it can be observed that the eligibility algorithm was executed 3 
times, once for each service agreement.
Solution Design
In the Bill Generation routine (CIPBBILG), limit execution of the Customer Class – Bill Eligibility 
algorithms to only the initial group of service agreements (or the first service agreement) 
processed, so that bill eligibility is evaluated upfront at the start of billing.

Description
When updating standalone Field Activities (no parent) the Update Orchestrator created is not linked to Field

occurs specifically when those columns have null values in the database. As a result, export file

Submit the initial export batch job. Make sure "Do Not Apply Redaction Rules" set to Y.
Review the output JSON file once the batch job is successful.
Expected: Numeric columns with null values should appear in the JSON file.

Description
Health assessment calculation returns 0 as the "Percentage to Failure" value when the 
assessment result is Fail.
This incorrect value occurs in the following scenario:
The Measured Value is greater than or equal to the Fail Limit, and
The Assessment Score is not set by the algorithm that calculates the Measured Value.
Steps To Recreate
Select or create a Health Assessment Type where the Health Assessment Type algorithm 
calculates a Measured Value that is greater than or equal to the Fail Limit. Also, ensure the 
algorithm does not set the Assessment Score.
Run the Health Assessment Monitor batch (F1ASMNT).
After the batch completes, review the latest health assessment for that Health Assessment Type.
Expected: Percentage to Failure should be 100.
Actual: Percentage to Failure is 0.

Reported Issue

Description
Steps To Recreate
Description
There is a mismatch with fields describing the formatInstructions to get summary of a doctype 
with AIA in the schema of data area: F1-AIGenericSummarizationParm
 <formatInstructions type="group" mapXML="XML_SOURCE">
 <length mdField="F1_SUMM_LEN_FLG" dataType="lookup" 
lookup="F1_SUMM_LEN_FLG"/>
 <format mdField="F1_SUMM_FRMT_FLG" dataType="lookup" 
lookup="F1_SUMM_FRMT_FLG"/>
 </formatInstructions>
The AIA rest endpoint used to summarize doctype expects this in the following format in JSON:
"format_instructions": {
 "length": "short",
 "summary_format": "bullet"
 }
Steps To Recreate
Make a service call to summarize a docType with AIA rest endpoint. The summary result of the

Note: This issue reproduces in C2M/CCS. In C2M dev , replication was achieved by following

Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing 38945318 Product Fix Design
Solution Design
The fix is implemented in the translated Java routine RateApplicationProcessorService. Two 
methods that populate the Rate Check result payload are updated:
1. createList_READ_LIST
For each read, the measured quantity and register quantity are read from the Bill 
Segment Read DTO. If either value has a scale greater than 6, it is replaced with the 
result of RoundingHelper.scaleFullValue for the appropriate field name (MSR_QTY, 
FINAL_REG_QTY), so that the value passed to the GTT has at most 6 decimal places.
2. createList_SQ_LIST
For each service quantity, the billable service quantity and initial service quantity are read 
from the Bill Segment Service Quantity DTO. If either has a scale greater than 6, it is 
replaced with the result of RoundingHelper.scaleFullValue for BILL_SQ and INIT_SQ 
respectively.
No database schema changes, admin table changes, or UI changes are required. The change is 
limited to the Java service that builds the read and SQ lists for Rate Check so that the data 
conforms to the existing GTT scale of 6.

Reported Issue
Description
When Usage subscription has two Dynamic option types configured for the same duration and 
both the Dynamic Options has respective TOU maps then TOU map related to one is getting 
picked up.
Currently Two Dynamic Options are configured for the TOU map, if both dynamic Options are 
present on the usage subscription as well for the bill duration then associated SQI/TOU 
combination from both dynamic options/TOU Map combination should appear in usage 
transaction.
Steps to Recreate
1) Create required V set up for Interval MC.
2) Create “Get TOU Mapped” usage group/rule with Enforce US Dynamic Option is Yes.
3) Configure the usage group to the US Type.
4) Create TOU Map with dynamic options configured.
5) Generate TOU Map data and Interval measurements.
6) Create a Usage Subscription with effective Dynamic options configured and NO Dynamic

Reported Issue
Description
BCS generates bill with multiple headers when there is a rate change within a billing period
When an SA has a Rate change within a billing period, BCS generates bill segment with multiple 
headers (one for each Rate schedule) in spite of SA Type configuration set up to select the rate at
the start of the billing period.
When an SA has multiple rate schedules within the billing period:
 The base algorithm “Derive Usage Group based on Rate & Installed Device” selects 
multiple Usage Groups based on the rate schedules.
 This results in the creation of multiple Sub UTs.
 Consequently, multiple Bill Calculation headers are generated—one per rate schedule.
 This occurs even though the SA Type is configured to select a single rate, effectively 
overriding the SA Type configuration during usage calculation.

1.Reported Issue
Description
A customer has described a problem in which a remote connect or remote disconnect activity fails with a 
system error. The error is caused by the head end system returning none of the critical information required 
by the process, but such an error should not be catastrophic to the activity.
Solution Design
The Evaluate Response lifecycle state of the D7-ConnectDisconnectResultDR is the correct place to check 
the head end system’s response and mitigate any errors. This particular error could potentially be fixed by a 
simple retry of the “Get Results” communication. However, the Evaluate Response state only transitions to 
the Create Completion Events and Discarded states. The state should be modified to allow also transitions to 
the Response Error state. Then, the D7-EVLCDRESP script should check for missing elements in the 
response. When missing elements are discovered, it should create a log message and transition the BO 
instance to Response Error.
Because the D7-MeterReadResultsInterval, D7-MeterReadResultsScalar, and D7-PingResultsDR BOs are 
similarly structured, they should also be updated to allow Evaluate Response to transition to Response Error. 
Since the head end is not expected to truncate the results from these commands, no script modifications are 
required for these BO

To address the C1-BLCMP performance issue, the 
BillCompletionUpdateMDMUsageInfoFromCobolWrapper flow should be changed so that it does 
not invoke the C1-UpdMDMUsI service script during bill completion for C2M. This script can 
continue to run in its separate instance where applicable.
Instead, introduce a new SQL-based approach, like the existing logic, to identify the relevant 
Usage Requests and derive the corresponding Usage Transactions by joining through 
USG_EXT_ID, which stores the Usage Request ID and is indexed on the UT side.

both 'N'. These are cases typically already handled when the FT freeze algorithm 
C1UPDMDMUFTF is plugged in. 
 For Bill Segment (BS) financial transactions, exclude records where both flags are 
already 'Y'. This avoids redundant updates in scenarios where a completed bill is 
reopened and then completed again.

Reported Issue
Description
Unable to migrate data for maintenance object Usage (C1-USAGE) due to invalid values for the 
data conversion roles of its tables.
Steps To Recreate

Maintenance Object - C1-USAGE
C1-USAGE – Table Information
4 Copyright ©2026, Oracle. All rights reserved.

Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing Bug 39064768 Product Fix Design
Expected Result: The tables that are needed to be converted has Data conversion role of 
‘Convert’.
Actual Result: The Data conversion role is ‘Not Converted’.
Solution Design
 Update the Data Conversion Role value of the Usage (C1_USAGE) primary table from ‘Not 
Converted’ to ‘Convert (New PK)’ so that the created Batch Controls can process the table 
properly.
 Update the Data Conversion Role value of the Usage Characteristic (C1_USAGE_CHAR) 
child table from ‘Not Converted’ to ‘Convert (Retain PK)’ so that the created Batch Controls 
can process the table properly.
 Update the Data Conversion Role value of the Usage Log (C1_USAGE_LOG) child table 
from ‘Not Converted’ to ‘Convert (Retain PK)’ so that the created Batch Controls can process 
the table properly.
 Update the Data Conversion Role value of the Usage Log Message Parameter 
(C1_USAGE_LOG_PARM) child table from ‘Not Converted’ to ‘Convert (Retain PK)’ so that 
the created Batch Controls can process the table properly.
 Create the Conversion Batch Controls by using the Maintenance Object Configuration

common data issues in preliminary runs. 
Errors encountered during validation are logged onto the 
conversion error table. Note that at the start of this job, 
all rows in the conversion error table for the process

Reported Issue
Contents
Description
Steps To Recreate
Description
In a Data Explorer popup, when a search request fails due to insufficient prefilled hidden filters 
causing an error, the popup remains stuck in the loading state. The loading animation continues 
to display and blocks the input fields, preventing the user from performing another search.
Steps To Recreate
Add a Maintenance Map with a search field that launches a Data Explorer popup with prefilled 
hidden filters. If the hidden filters do not provide sufficient search criteria, the request returns an 
insufficient search criteria error. In this case, the loading animation persists and is not removed, 
preventing the user from performing further searches as the animation blocks the search fields.
For example in the WAM Application:
1. Navigate to "Add Asset"
2. Select any asset type
3. Click the search icon to select asset location. This will open a data explorer popup.
Verify that after the initial load with hidden filters, the popup's loading animation is removed, 
allowing the user to perform searches.

Solution Design
Summary
Usage Group selected would be associated with the Rate that was in effect at the beginning of 
the UT period. 
When an SA has a rate change within a billing period and the SA Type is configured to select the 
rate effective at the start of the billing period, BCS should:
 Apply only one rate schedule for the entire bill period
 Use a single Usage Group (No Sub UT’s created)

updated to pick the Rate that is in effect

Only the service points whose stop date/time is greater than usage transaction start date/time are considered. Due to this usage for single day closing bill, where the usage transaction starts on the usage subscription end date/time, is not calculated.

Reported Issue
Description
After upgrading CC&B from 2.7 to 25.4, billing behavior changed for Customer Class Bill Eligibility 
algorithms. In 2.7, these eligibility algorithms executed only once per account during billing, and if 
any eligibility algorithm encountered an error and created a To Do, the bill segment creation was 
rolled back, and eligibility processing stopped.
In 25.4, the same eligibility algorithms are executed multiple times for the same account - typically 
once per billable Service Agreement (SA) within the account - because the billing process loops 
through SAs and repeatedly calls the billing routine that evaluates eligibility. Additionally, error 
handling differs when an eligibility algorithm creates a To Do in 25.4, billing is not rolled back and 
subsequent eligibility algorithms continue to run, allowing billing to proceed.

for each SA.

irrespective of the number of service agreements it has.

algorithms to only the initial group of service agreements (or the first service agreement) 
processed, so that bill eligibility is evaluated upfront at the start of billing.

1. Reported Issue
Description
When updating standalone Field Activities (no parent) the Update Orchestrator created is not linked to Field 
Activity. Update orchestrator is created but not shown when viewing the originating activity.
Steps To Recreate
1. Initiate FA/D1-ReadMeter for current date and SP ID 12345 (address = LL11)
2. FA initiated, FA O/B communication is created and moved to Awaiting Response.
3. On FA page click on Initiate Update.
4. Fill out required fields and save.
5. Update Orchestration activity is created.
6. Navigate back to Field Activity.
7. Issue: no Update Orchestration activity listed in Hierarchy tree.
8. The user must search for Update Orchestration activity.
Investigation
Problem Cause
The current system has a limitation where it only populates Orchestration activities related to "Request 
Orchestrator activities". The defect requires enhancing the system components to also populate in the activity 
tree, cancel, or update Orchestration activities related to "Field Activity".
Suggested Solution
The fix is to provide functionality to populate. Cancel\Update Orchestration activities related to Field Activity.

Reported Issue
Description
The view is connecting the device config to all locations it’s been installed and because of that 
displays same field activity more once instead of the single instance for the correct premise 
where the configuration is actually installed.
Unable to use the existing view, will need to recreate the query in the view manually.
The view is needed for the report that is used for electric outage management.
Steps To Recreate

select *
from X1_BI_ACTIVITY_VW

The issue was reproduced when the same device was connected to multiple SPs at different

Reported Issue
Description
When running the Asset Monitor Batch Control with more than one thread, the status shows the 
number of records processed as more than the records that should be processed. 
Steps to Recreate
Data Requirements
 Asset records to be processed for a specific Asset Type. Search for the Assets with this 
Asset Type in the application or from the database.
Steps Scenario 1
Navigate to the Batch Job Submission by navigating to Main Menu, Tools, Batch Job Submission. 
Add or search for an existing Batch Code W1-ASSET and duplicate the record. Add the Asset 
Type Batch Job Parameter to limit the number of records processed since too many records may 
take an excessive amount of time. Within the Main section, specify a thread count of at least 2. 
Click Save to start the Batch Job Submission.
4 Copyright ©2025, Oracle. All rights reserved.

Product Fix Design
Expected Results for Scenario 1
The status of the Batch Run shows the number of Processed Records the same as number of 
asset records with the Asset Type from Data Requirements. From the Batch Run portal, Threads 
tab, the total number of records processed across all threads is the same as the total number of 
asset records. 
Actual Results for Scenario 1
The status of the Batch Run shows the number of Processed Records the same as twice the 
number of asset records with the Asset Type from Data Requirements. From the Batch Run 
portal, Threads tab, the total number of records processed across all threads is twice as much as 
the total number of asset records.
Investigation
Problem Cause
Within the backing Java program for the Batch Control, the query to retrieve the Asset records 
was missing the filter for the low and high values. This filter

Investigation
Problem Cause
Within the backing Java program for the Batch Control, the query to retrieve the Asset records 
was missing the filter for the low and high values. This filter is used by Framework logic to specify 
the range of records to process for the thread.
Suggested Solution
Modify the backing Java program to include the low and high filters.

Description
The Generalized Initial Export (GDE) omits numeric columns from json export files. Omission 
occurs specifically when those columns have null values in the database. As a result, export file 
lack certain numeric fields if they are null.
Steps To Recreate
Ensure the data to be exported includes numeric columns with null values. For example, the 
D1_SP table has numeric columns D1_GEO_LAT and D1_GEO_LONG that can contain nulls.
Enable the initial export for the D1-SP maintenance object.
Submit the initial export batch job. Make sure "Do Not Apply Redaction Rules" set to Y.
Review the output JSON file once the batch job is successful.
Expected: Numeric columns with null values should appear in the JSON file.
Actual: Numeric columns with null values are missing from the JSON file.

Bug 38765121 Product Fix Design Oracle Utilities Meter Data Management
Reported Issue
Description
Baseline Calculation is expecting Temperature Interval size and Meter Read Interval size to be 
same. In general, weather data is provided in hourly intervals and meter data can be of different 
interval sizes.
Steps To Recreate
N/A
Solution Design
 Baseline calculation has been enhanced to support a different interval size for 
temperature – 
 A new field ‘Temperature Interval Size’ has been added.
 If Interval size > Temperature interval size, then error is thrown during the baseline 
calculation.
 If Interval size < Temperature interval size,
o Align the temperature windows to the meter reads - aligned measurement 
window.
o These dates are then used to retrieve the temperature measurements.
 The logic used to determine whether an event occurred on a given day has been updated
to also consider the event participation. As a result, in the logic, an event is now 
considered to have occurred on a day only when the program event includes event 
participation. Such days are skipped.
 Changes have been made to align the time component with the interval size for adjusted 
baseline measurements and raw baseline measurements.

Description
In fixed-position extract files, space padding is applied based on byte length rather than character
count.
When the data contains multilingual characters (for example, Chinese), this results in fields not 
occupying the expected number of character positions.
As a result, although the extract completes successfully, the output file may appear visually 
misaligned when reviewed, leading to concerns about field positioning.
Steps To Recreate
1.Configure an extract batch using a fixed-position format (FIXD).
2.Populate one or more fields of table being queried with multilingual (Unicode) characters.
3.Run the extract to generate the output file.
4.Review the generated file in a text editor.
Output:
The column containing multilingual characters ends before its expected position.

Bug 38721796 Product Fix Design Oracle Utilities Framework
Description
Several enhancements are implemented in the To Do Management portal as well as the Details 
tab of the To Do Dashboard portal.
- Open up the restriction that currently requires either To Do Type or Assignee. Users may now 
enter a To Do Role without other criteria. Note that it is recommended to use the To Do Role 
filter by itself for use cases where a reasonable number of records are associated.
- As part of this, the dependency between the To Do Role and the To Do Type are adjusted. 
When selecting a To Do Role, the list of To Do Types are those valid for the Role. Similarly when
selecting a To Do Type, the list of To Do Roles are those valid for the Type.
- The Characteristic Type filters are now available when selecting To Do Role only. In this case, 
the system shows all the Characteristic Types that are valid for the To Do Entity. If you select a 
To Do Type and the To Do Type has valid To Do characteristic types defined, the existing logic 
applies where the system shows only the Char Types for the To Do Type. For manual To Do 
Types, the list is always built based on the values defined on the To Do Type.
- In addition, the values for characteristic filters are now retained when a to do type is changed as
long as the characteristic type is valid for the new to do type.

c filters are now retained when a to do type is changed as
long as the characteristic type is valid for the new to do type. 
- There is a new opt-in feature related to displaying the Characteristics column in the results. 
Currently this column shows name / value pairs of characteristics linked to the To Do Entry. If a 
To Do Entry has many characteristics linked to it, the row takes up more vertical space to show 
all the values. It means that fewer To Do entries are visible in the list. As part of this fix, you can 
opt in to setting this value to be collapsed by default. To enable the collapsing, go to Admin > 
General Options > Feature Configuration. Search for an existing feature configuration with the 
Feature Type 'Activity Queue Management'. If one does not exist, create a feature configuration 
of this type. Select the 'Collapse Characteristics Column' option and set the value to Y (Yes).
In addition, two fixes are included in this enhancement:
- The message filter often caused a horizontal scroll if the message text is too long. This is fixed.
- When the filter criteria match a very large number of records (tens of thousands of records or 
more), users may have received a timeout. In this release, we implemented a fetch limit of 5000 
to forestall any timeouts. Using the To Do Dashboard you are able to see counts of records by 
certain criteria. If a Role or a To Do Type has a large number of records, users should put as 
much filter criteria as possible to be sure to get the data they are looking for.

FW Changes
Changes were made to the zones for the To Do Management portal and the Details tab on the To
Do Dashboard portal per the description.
Recommended Test Cases
For an environment with existing To Do Entries, confirm the following:
- A user can select a To Do Role and search for To Do entries for that role across To Do types.
- When selecting only a To Do Role, the Characteristic Type filters are built and a user can 
search for To Do entries that reference the Char Type / Char Value populated. All the 
characteristic types that are valid for the 'To Do Entry' characteristic entity are listed.
- When selecting a To Do Role, the To Do Type dropdown shows only the To Do Types that are 
valid for the role.
- Selecting a To Do Type no longer resets a value populated in the filter for the To Do Role. The 
To Do Role dropdown only shows the To Do Roles that are valid for the type.
- Selecting a To Do Type no longer resets the characteristic type filters - if the populated 
characteristic type is also valid for the seleted To Do Type
- When selecting a To Do Type that has valid To Do Entry characteristic types defined, only those
characteristic types are shown in the dropdown (existing behavior)
- The message text filter continues to only be available when a To Do Type is found. However, 
longer text should no longer cause a horizontal scroll for the left column of filters.
For the characteristic column in the results, the previous behavior should be observed by default. 
All the characteristics are listed as name / value pairs.

Reported Issue
Description
The Retrieve Most Recent Payment (C1-RETMRPYMT) Business Service incorrectly identifies 
the "latest payment" by excluding payments made on the current day if they were posted after 
midnight. This results in outdated financial details being presented to the user immediately after a 
payment is made.
Steps To Recreate
 Find/Create an account with multiple frozen payments on the same day.
Multiple frozen payments exist on 2026-01-08 for account
 Verify that one of the payment FT’s Freeze Date/Time should be set exactly in midnight of the 
same day.
4 Copyright ©2026, Oracle. All rights reserved.

Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing Bug 38883139 Product Fix Design
Take note of the Payment ID (Parent ID) on FT. Freeze Date/Time is set to midnight.
 On the Override User System Date Zone, Set the Override Date to match the Payment Date
 Test the Retrieve Most Recent Payment (C1-RETMRPYMT) Business Service using the 
Financial Details Service (C1FinDetails) Service Script with the Account ID and “HTTP 
Method” set to Get.
Expected Result: The latest payment as of the provided Current Date value is shown.
Actual Result: The payment posted exactly at midnight of the day is shown, even though there 
are later payments made within the day.
Copyright ©2026, Oracle. All rights reserved. 5

Bug 38883139 Product Fix Design Oracle Utilities Customer Care and Billing
Payment post exactly at midnight of the day is shown

Update the SQL query in the Retrieve Most Recent Payment (C1-RETMRPYMT) Business 
Service to apply the TRUNC function to the payment freeze date-time column. This truncates the 
value to a date-only format (midnight) before comparison, ensuring it matches the granularity of 
the input date and correctly includes same-day payments.

This enhancement is to backport the below features from 26.4 to 25.10 version.
1. We can associate a Service Point to a Weather Data source using a weather source 
identifier, enabling standardized access to weather data across DACS and MDM. By 
leveraging a weather source identifier stored on the Service Point, the system will 
dynamically resolve and link to the appropriate weather data channel. The primary goal is
to ensure consistent weather data mapping for use in estimation, billing, and settlement 
workflows.

Reported Issue
Description
The view is connecting the device config to all locations it’s been installed and because of that 
displays same field activity more once instead of the single instance for the correct premise 
where the configuration is actually installed.
Unable to use the existing view, will need to recreate the query in the view manually.
The view is needed for the report that is used for electric outage management.
Steps To Recreate
1. Run the following query using the X1_BI_ACTIVITY_VW view:
select *
from X1_BI_ACTIVITY_VW 
where d1_activity_id = '85573036879904';
2. This is expected to return one record for the location that the activity is associated to.
3. But it returns two records for different premises and service points.
Investigation
Problem Cause
The issue was reproduced when the same device was connected to multiple SPs at different 
times.
Suggested Solution
The fix should be this part of SQL
left join (select distinct D1_DEVICE_ID, IE.D1_SP_ID, 
 IE.D1_INSTALL_DTTM, IE.D1_REMOVAL_DTTM
 from D1_DVC_CFG DC
 inner join D1_INSTALL_EVT IE on IE.DEVICE_CONFIG_ID = DC.DEVICE_CONFIG_ID
 ) DS on DS.D1_DEVICE_ID = AD.PK_VALUE1 
 and DS.D1_INSTALL_DTTM <= AC.CRE_DTTM
 and (DS.D1_REMOVAL_DTTM is null or DS.D1_REMOVAL_DTTM >= AC.CRE_DTTM)

Description
Starting with 25.10, stricter validation was introduced for file names and extensions uploaded 
through the system (including batch driven uploads and attachments).
As part of this enhancement, the framework validates file extensions against a managed content 
allowlist (F1-FileExtensionAllowList).
After upgrading to 25.10, customers reported that certain file extensions that were previously 
accepted are now rejected during batch processing.
This fix is to introduce support for implementations to add to the system's allowlist for file 
extensions.
Steps To Recreate
1. Upload a file attachment from the "Add Attachment" page.
2. Ensure the extension being used is not present in managed content F1-FileExtensionAllowList.
3. Observe that the upload process rejects the file due to extension validation failure.

Description
Users are unable to use the concatenateGroovyStrings method to build string literals that include 
dynamic integer index values. One use case is generating bind variable names for primary keys, 
where an integer from 1 to 5 can be appended based on how many primary key columns a table 
has.
Copyright ©2026, Oracle. All rights reserved. 3

Bug 38627909 Product Fix Design Oracle Utilities Framework
Steps To Recreate
Create a new Groovy script that builds a query to fetch records from the database. The script 
should constructs the SQL using the concatenateGroovyStrings method and generate bind 
variable names dynamically based on the number of primary key columns in the table.
Determine the number of primary key columns, then use a for loop to append integer index value 
to column names and bind variables using concatenateGroovyStrings. When you click Save, the 
application throws an error indicating that integers are not allowed as arguments to 
concatenateGroovyStrings.
Example:
String sql = concatenateGroovyStrings("SELECT * FROM F1_MO_UPD WHERE ")
for (int i = 1; i <= pkCount; i++) {
 sql = concatenateGroovyStrings(sql, "PK_VALUE", i, " = ", ":pkVal", i)
 if (i < pkCount) {
 sql = concatenateGroovyStrings(sql, " AND ")
 }
}
def query = createPreparedStatement(sql, "comment")

Issue 1

Where the expectation is that it should be the date/time of when the To Do entry was most

Issue 2

2. Re-Open the To To Entry
3. Later - Re-assign the To Do Entry Back to the Original User
Example
Log Seq and Type Log Date Assigned User Expected Last Assigned Date/Time

2 Assigned 3rd Jan USER1 3rd Jan

4 Assigned 8th Jan USER1 8th Jan
The "Latest Assigned Date/Time" will display as the 3rd of Jan, When It should show 8th of Jan.

Make changes so that it will calculate the latest assigned date/time based on both the assigned

Reported Issue
Description
When Usage subscription has two Dynamic option types configured for the same duration and 
both the Dynamic Options has respective TOU maps then TOU map related to one is getting 
picked up.
Currently Two Dynamic Options are configured for the TOU map, if both dynamic Options are 
present on the usage subscription as well for the bill duration then associated SQI/TOU 
combination from both dynamic options/TOU Map combination should appear in usage 
transaction.
Steps to Recreate
1) Create required V set up for Interval MC.
2) Create “Get TOU Mapped” usage group/rule with Enforce US Dynamic Option is Yes.
3) Configure the usage group to the US Type.
4) Create TOU Map with dynamic options configured.
5) Generate TOU Map data and Interval measurements.
6) Create a Usage Subscription with effective Dynamic options configured and NO Dynamic
Option Overrides. 
7) Add the usage group to the US
8) Configure Dynamic options on the TOU Map.
9) Create a UT.
10) Only one of the Dynamic Options configured on the TOU Map is applied in UT.
Solution Design
Apply TOU Mapping business component
 The code change is in the ApplyTOUMapping_Impl.java common routine to convert 
Usage Subscription - Dynamic Option and Dynamic Opt. Override date/times from legal 
to standard and compare against Dynamic Option effective and expiration date/times. Fix 
is in enforceUSDynamicOptions(...) method.

Bug 39002995 Product Fix Design Oracle Utilities Service and Measurement Data Foundation
Reported Issue
Description
BCS generates bill with multiple headers when there is a rate change within a billing period
When an SA has a Rate change within a billing period, BCS generates bill segment with multiple 
headers (one for each Rate schedule) in spite of SA Type configuration set up to select the rate at
the start of the billing period.
When an SA has multiple rate schedules within the billing period:
 The base algorithm “Derive Usage Group based on Rate & Installed Device” selects 
multiple Usage Groups based on the rate schedules.
 This results in the creation of multiple Sub UTs.
 Consequently, multiple Bill Calculation headers are generated—one per rate schedule.
 This occurs even though the SA Type is configured to select a single rate, effectively 
overriding the SA Type configuration during usage calculation.

Solution Design
Summary
When an SA has a rate change within a billing period and the SA Type is configured to select the 
rate effective at the start of the billing period, BCS should:
 Apply only one rate schedule for the entire bill period
 Generate a single Bill Segment header
 Use a single Usage Group (No Sub UT’s created), regardless of mid-period rate changes

Solution Design
 Update the subsequent program logic to reference the returned count result instead of 
directly relying on the existence of a single SQL result row. When the count is greater than 
zero, proceed with Override Consumption Period logic; otherwise bypass it and use default 
billing consumption logic.
 Modify the translated COBOL programs CIPBUSPX and CIPBDCPN to replace the direct 
single-row lookup against CI_SA_TYPE_CHAR with a COUNT(*)-based check. This ensures 
that scenarios with multiple SA Types across CIS Divisions do not trigger a SQL error due to 
multiple row retrievals.

Reported Issue
Description
Rate Change in middle of period (Rate change a day after bill segment start date). The 
regenerated bill segment comes with 1 bseg header only covering the new rate schedule (missing
the old rate schedule).
When there is rate change on usage subscription that falls on the last day of billing, the usage 
transaction ends in issue for the last day as it is requiring a read to be present on the subUT 
created for the rate change.

DRVUSGGRP) has Suppress One Day Effective Rates (Y/N) = Y

o Ensure rate change happens on 2-1-2025
o Ensure interval and scalar present on device

12:00AM
 Ensure scalar MC has reads for 01-01-2025 12:00AM and 02-01-2025 
12:00AM
3. Create usage transaction for dates
o Interval Start 01-01-2025 12:00AM
o Interval End From 02-02-2025 12:00AM
o Interval End To 02-02-2025 12:00AM
o Scalar Start 01-01-2025 12:00AM
o Scalar End From 02-01-2025 12:00AM
o Scalar End To 02-01-2025 11:59AM
Verify that UT is processed and subUT is created for 1 day period.

1.Reported Issue
Description
A customer has described a problem in which a remote connect or remote disconnect activity fails with a 
system error. The error is caused by the head end system returning none of the critical information required 
by the process, but such an error should not be catastrophic to the activity.
Solution Design
The Evaluate Response lifecycle state of the D7-ConnectDisconnectResultDR is the correct place to check 
the head end system’s response and mitigate any errors. This particular error could potentially be fixed by a 
simple retry of the “Get Results” communication. However, the Evaluate Response state only transitions to 
the Create Completion Events and Discarded states. The state should be modified to allow also transitions to 
the Response Error state. Then, the D7-EVLCDRESP script should check for missing elements in the 
response. When missing elements are discovered, it should create a log message and transition the BO 
instance to Response Error.
Because the D7-MeterReadResultsInterval, D7-MeterReadResultsScalar, and D7-PingResultsDR BOs are 
similarly structured, they should also be updated to allow Evaluate Response to transition to Response Error. 
Since the head end is not expected to truncate the results from these commands, no script modifications are 
required for these B

Reported Issue
Description
For commercial program, the Settlement Transaction created "after Event" will be moved to 
CALC-DEFER status (since the amount calculation will be deferred). Once a Settlement is moved 
to calculation deferred status, there are cases where meter reads can be corrected and there is 
no way to RECALCULATE these transactions since CALC-DEFER is defined as FINAL status. 
Steps to Recreate
1. Create Program Settlement Calculation Group with End of Event program settlement rule.
a. Defer Amount Calculation = Yes
b. UOM = KW
2. Create Program / Program event.
a. Configure Program Settlement Calculation Group
3. Create Program Subscription.
a. Configure Program
4. Create an EST. It is transitioned to “Calculation Deferred” state
5. Observe that there is no way to RECALCULATE EST since CALC-DEFER is defined as 
FINAL status.

specified MSP, but in addition, subscriptions for other MSPs associated with the specified

Location but match the supplied Metered Service.
